decisions.reason: The source's Hero V terminal change and geometry-preservation constraint are already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The requested terminal comparison format, dimensions, purpose, variation count, and geometry constraint are already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The source's second-V terminal change and preservation of its established structure and slope are already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The source preserves the second V's established geometry and does not change its height relationship to the E, L, Hero V, or É accent.

The existing MODIFY captures the new terminal style but leaves a stale exclusivity rule stating that the expressive signature is reserved to the Hero V and É accent, although the source now applies the shared refined terminal to the second V as well.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

After comparing the kerning studies together, I am definitely most attracted to Option 2 (Balanced Flow). It reads as one unified word but still retains the airiness and elegance we have been developing.

Before proceeding with the material treatments, I want to reconsider the terminal used by the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

We devoted substantial time to perfecting the Hero V before the rest of the alphabet had been created. At that point, the Hero V had to express far more of the identity by itself. With the complete wordmark now assembled, I no longer think it needs to be so expressive or decorative.

I’m seeking a feeling of precision, assurance, and quiet elevation. I’d like to test a terminal that appears more deliberate and architectural—a restrained, controlled upward release instead of a flourish.

I’m attaching two references that start to convey the quality I mean. I do not want either one reproduced exactly, but their cleaner transitions and more restrained elevation appeal to me.

The established structure and slope of both the Hero V and second V should remain unchanged. Instead, please create a few interpretations that preserve that geometry while applying a consistently refined terminal to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

Thank you!

value_updates.terminal_style: Use the same deliberate, architectural, restrained, and controlled upward-release terminal as the Hero V rather than an expressive or decorative flourish.

decisions.reason: The source explicitly confines exploration to the shared terminal of the Hero V, second V, and É accent while keeping every other established design decision unchanged.
Refining the shared terminal does not alter the existing requirement that the É accent and Hero V peaks share the same horizontal reference line.
The source's selection of Option 2 Balanced Flow is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY, and the subsequent terminal study does not change that kerning selection.
Changing the geometry of the shared terminal does not change which signature elements receive champagne gold or the black treatment of the remaining elements.
The source postpones proceeding with material treatment while studying terminals but does not change the selected Satin Reflection finish or its required character.
The terminal refinement preserves the established V structures and does not change the shared baseline alignment.
The terminal design decision has no effect on the accepted formats used to deliver accessible review images.
